comment: Endgame trainer curriculum (ROADMAP Phase 5). Structure only — a
rating-banded progression from essential positions to harder technique
— is inspired by the classic endgame-course format; every position,
title and instruction below is original or centuries-old public-domain
theory (Lucena, Philidor, opposition, the square of the pawn, key
squares, Vancura, ...), described in our own words.
Every FEN's theoretical result was verified against Syzygy tablebases
one exception is pawn-breakthrough (8 men, beyond the 7-man tables):
the centuries-old three-abreast breakthrough, with both capture
branches and both decline branches verified by hand. shouldering-race
is the public-domain game Schlage-Ahues, Berlin 1921 (with Maizelis's
winning king route) at its critical white-to-move moment. The side to
move in each FEN is the side the user plays; `goal` is the theoretical
result the user must achieve. `material` is white-vs-black piece

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.summary: The two basic mates, the square of the pawn, king-and-pawn fundamentals every player must know cold, and the stalemate traps that undo them.

tiers.name: Building technique
tiers.summary: Opposition in all its forms, key squares, spare tempi, queen against a pawn on the seventh, outside passers, and knowing when to trade into a pawn ending.

tiers.name: Rook endings and tempo play
tiers.summary: The rook endings that decide practical games — Lucena, Philidor, Vancura and their rescue setups — plus pawn breakthroughs, king races, and tempo maneuvering.

drills.title: Queen mate: king on the edge
drills.instruction: Shrink the defending king's space with the queen a knight's-move away, bring your own king up, and mate on the edge — watch for stalemate.

drills.title: Queen mate: king in the center
drills.instruction: First push the centralized king to any edge with the queen alone, then walk your king over to finish.

drills.title: Rook mate: shrink the box
drills.instruction: Confine the king behind a rook barrier, march your king up square by square, and tighten the box until mate on the edge.

drills.title: Rook mate: cut off first
drills.instruction: Use the rook to fence the king into one half of the board before advancing your own king — the cut-off does most of the work.

drills.title: The square of the pawn: catch it
drills.instruction: Picture the square drawn from the pawn to its promotion rank: if your king can step inside it, the pawn is caught. Step in and run it down.

drills.title: The square of the pawn: outrun the king
drills.instruction: The defending king stands outside the pawn's square. Push immediately — every pawn step redraws a smaller square it can never enter — then finish with the queen.

drills.title: King two ranks ahead of its pawn
drills.instruction: With the king leading its pawn by two ranks the win never slips: advance the king first, take the opposition when the kings meet, and push the pawn last.

drills.title: King on the sixth, pawn behind
drills.instruction: A king on the sixth rank in front of its pawn wins regardless of whose move it is. Sidestep, let the defender commit, and shepherd the pawn home.

drills.title: Hold the draw with the opposition
drills.instruction: Meet the enemy king head-on and keep the opposition; when the pawn steps forward, plant your king directly in its path and never get pushed aside.

drills.title: Rook pawn: the corner is a fortress
drills.instruction: Against a rook pawn the promotion corner is unbreakable: shuffle between the corner and the square beside it — any eviction attempt ends in stalemate.

drills.title: Rook pawn: wrong side of the board
drills.instruction: The defending king starts a file too far from the queening corner. Run the pawn before the king crosses — then mate with the new queen.

drills.title: Win the queen ending without stalemating
drills.instruction: The pawn hangs, but grabbing it leaves the trapped king without a single legal move. Let the defender keep that one breathing hole and close in for mate — greed here is the only way to spoil the win.

drills.title: Distant opposition
drills.instruction: With kings far apart, claim the distant opposition — an odd number of squares between the kings with the opponent to move — and convert it to the close opposition as you advance.

drills.title: Save the pawn moves
drills.instruction: The pawn far behind your king is a bank of spare tempi. Improve the king to its key squares first; spend a pawn step only when you need the defender to move.

drills.title: Outflanking
drills.instruction: You already hold the opposition — use it: when the defender gives way, step diagonally around, gaining ground rank by rank until the pawn can run.

drills.title: Blockade the sixth-rank pawn
drills.instruction: The pawn reached the sixth ahead of its king. Retreat straight back onto the promotion path, take the opposition when the king steps up, and remember: stalemate is your friend.

drills.title: Attacker's king trails its pawn
drills.instruction: While the pawn leads its own king you can hold: blockade it, and each time the enemy king advances, meet it head-on with the opposition.

drills.title: Queen vs pawn on the seventh: center pawn
drills.instruction: Approach with checks and pins until the defending king is forced onto the square in front of its own pawn — that frozen moment buys your king one step closer. Repeat until the king arrives.

drills.title: Queen vs pawn on the seventh: knight pawn
drills.instruction: Same winning ladder as against a center pawn: check, force the king in front of the pawn, gain a king step, repeat — a knight pawn offers no stalemate tricks.

drills.title: Rook pawn on the seventh holds the queen
drills.instruction: Stay beside your pawn. Whenever the queen forces your king in front of it, that is stalemate — so no tempo is ever gained and the far-away king never arrives.

drills.title: Bishop pawn on the seventh holds the queen
drills.instruction: Head for the corner next to your pawn: if the queen ever takes it, the position is stalemate. That standing threat stops the winning ladder cold.

drills.title: The outside passer is a decoy
drills.instruction: Push the faraway pawn and make the defending king chase it; that pawn's job is to die far from the real battle. While it is being run down, march your own king the other way, harvest the frozen pawn, and promote.

drills.title: Trade rooks — the pawn ending is won
drills.instruction: The rooks stand face to face, and the whole position is one calculation: after the swap your king sits on a key square in front of its pawn. Work that pawn ending out to the end, then trade with confidence — retreating instead lets the defense escape.

drills.title: Lucena position: build the bridge
drills.instruction: Pawn on the seventh, your king stuck in front of it: place your rook on the fourth rank, step the king out, and when the checks come, walk it down and block with the rook — the bridge.

drills.title: Philidor position: the third-rank defense
drills.instruction: Keep your rook on your third rank so the enemy king can never camp there. The moment the pawn crosses, drop the rook behind it and check forever — the king has no shelter.

drills.title: Passive back-rank defense: knight pawn
drills.instruction: With a knight pawn this far advanced, the humble setup holds: king beside the promotion square, rook parked on the back rank. Stay put and let every breakthrough attempt bounce.

drills.title: Vancura draw vs the rook pawn
drills.instruction: Attack the pawn from the side along your third rank, keeping the enemy rook chained to it. When the king walks over to help, greet it with sideways checks it can never escape.

drills.title: Win with the king cut off
drills.instruction: Your rook fences the defending king far from the pawn. Keep the fence intact, escort the pawn with your king, and answer rear checks by walking toward the rook.

drills.title: Triangulation: hand back the move
drills.instruction: The direct approach square is covered by the pawn, and face-to-face the defender holds. Maneuver your king so the same standoff arrives with the other side to move — zugzwang wins the pawn.

drills.title: Wrong bishop, rook pawn
drills.instruction: The bishop does not control the promotion corner, so the corner is yours: shuttle between it and the neighboring square — driving you out stalemates, and the pawn never queens.

drills.title: Three-pawn breakthrough
drills.instruction: Three pawns stand shoulder to shoulder against three, and the kings are spectators: throw the middle pawn forward, answer either capture by sacrificing a second pawn on the far side, and the survivor walks through the cleared lane to promote.

drills.title: Shoulder the king out of the race
drills.instruction: Both kings sprint for the blocked pawns, but the straightest route is not the point: angle your king so each step toward the pawn also bars the defender from the saving corner. Win the pawn, then keep the late-arriving king at arm's length while yours steps aside to promote.

drills.title: Short side and checking distance
drills.instruction: The attacking king already leads its pawn, so the calm third-rank fence is gone. Your king belongs on the pawn's narrow side; your rook belongs far away on the other, checking across the full width of the board — three clear files of distance keep the checks alive forever.

drills.title: Rook behind the passer: the king walks in
drills.instruction: Your rook drives the pawn from behind and their rook is condemned to sit in front of it forever. Leave your rook exactly where it is — every tempo belongs to your king, which strolls across the board and evicts the blockader.

drills.title: Rook in front of the passer: hold the jail shut
drills.instruction: The enemy rook is imprisoned in front of its own pawn and yours guards the cell from behind. Never capture the pawn while its rook watches, keep your king tucked beside the corner, and when their king comes to free the prisoner, drive it off with checks from behind the pawn.

drills.title: Reroute into the Vancura stand
drills.instruction: With the pawn already on the sixth, hiding behind it will not save you forever. Bring the rook around to attack the pawn from the side — staying out of the approaching king's reach — so the pawn is nailed in place and your sideways checks stand ready when the king finally arrives.
